options.text: Forcing the browser to load all images at once for a smooth experience.

options.label: B
options.text: Writing code that runs in the background.

options.label: C
options.text: Delaying the loading of non-essential resources (like images below the fold) until the user scrolls to them.

options.label: D
options.text: Using multiple threads to run the browser.

explanation:
Lazy loading reduces initial page load time by only loading what is currently visible on the
screen. Images further down the page are only requested when the user scrolls near them.
subject: Web Development

question: (Code/Logic) The browser is trying to execute a script. Why does the code below likely slow down the page render?

options.label: A
options.text: The script is too large to fit in RAM.

options.label: B
options.text: It is a "parser-blocking" script; the browser must stop and download/execute it before it can continue building the DOM.

options.label: C
options.text: The browser requires a specific license to run it.

options.label: D
options.text: JavaScript is only allowed at the end of the body.

explanation:
Without async or defer, a <script> tag in the head causes the browser to "pause" HTML
parsing while the script is downloaded and executed, creating a visible delay for the user.
subject: Web Development

question: (Conceptual) Which HTTP 1.1 limitation is solved by Domain Sharding (an older, hacky trick for performance)?

options.label: A
options.text: The limitation that browsers limit the number of parallel connections to a single domain (usually to 6).

options.label: B
options.text: The inability to load images.

options.label: C
options.text: The lack of support for HTTPS.

options.label: D
options.text: The limitation of URL length.

explanation:
index.html
<head>
<script src="heavy-library.js"></script>
</head>
Browsers restrict concurrent downloads per domain. Developers used to host assets on
different subdomains (e.g., img1.site.com, img2.site.com) to trick the browser into
opening more concurrent connections. This is mostly unnecessary with HTTP/2.
subject: Web Development

question: (Calculation/Comparison) A page uses 3 high-res images (5MB each). If we enable compression (e.g., Brotli/Gzip), which metric is improved?

options.label: A
options.text: Network Latency

options.label: B
options.text: Payload Size

options.label: C
options.text: CSS Rendering Speed

options.label: D
options.text: DOM Tree Depth

explanation:
Compression reduces the actual number of bytes transferred over the network, making the
"payload" smaller. This helps lower the time-to-download, especially for slow connections.
subject: Web Development

question: (Conceptual) What is Tree Shaking in modern frontend frameworks (React/Vue)?

options.label: A
options.text: Removing all whitespace from CSS files.

options.label: B
options.text: Deleting the entire node_modules folder.

options.label: C
options.text: A process that eliminates "dead code" (unused functions/modules) from the final JavaScript bundle.

options.label: D
options.text: An animation technique to make buttons shake.

explanation:
If your app uses one small function from a massive library, Tree Shaking removes all the
unused parts of that library from your final build, making your file significantly smaller.
subject: Web Development

question: (Conceptual) What is the impact of CSS Bloat?

options.label: A
options.text: It increases the security of the page.

options.label: B
options.text: It increases the CSSOM construction time and causes the browser to download unnecessary rules.

options.label: C
options.text: It makes the browser engine faster.

options.label: D
options.text: It helps in SEO indexing.

explanation:
Every CSS rule is parsed by the browser. If you have 5,000 lines of CSS but only use 500, the
browser still spends CPU cycles parsing those unused rules, and the network spends time
downloading the unnecessary bytes.
subject: Web Development

question: (Conceptual) What is the primary purpose of using Breakpoints in a browser's DevTools during a debugging session?

options.label: A
options.text: To speed up the code execution.

options.label: B
options.text: To permanently delete problematic lines of code.

options.label: C
options.text: To pause code execution at a specific line, allowing the developer to inspect variables and the call stack.

options.label: D
options.text: To clear the browser cache.

explanation:
Breakpoints provide a "stop-frame" view of the application state, letting developers see exactly
what the data looks like at a specific moment in time.
subject: Web Development

question: (Scenario-Based) An API call is returning a 404 Not Found error, but the developer is sure the URL is correct. Which DevTools panel should be checked first?

options.label: A
options.text: Elements Panel

options.label: B
options.text: Console Panel

options.label: C
options.text: Network Panel

options.label: D
options.text: Application Panel

explanation:
The Network Panel tracks every HTTP request. It will show the exact URL being requested,
the headers, the payload, and the response code, which is essential for diagnosing API
communication issues.
subject: Web Development

question: (Comparison) What is the difference between Unit Testing and End-to-End (E2E) Testing?

options.label: A
options.text: Unit tests require a real browser; E2E tests are only for functions.

options.label: B
options.text: Unit tests focus on individual functions/components in isolation; E2E tests simulate a real user navigating through the entire application.

options.label: C
options.text: Unit tests are slower; E2E tests are faster.

options.label: D
options.text: Unit tests are more likely to fail.

explanation:
Unit tests are fast and verify specific logic. E2E tests are slower and prone to being "flaky," but
they provide the highest confidence that the entire user flow (e.g., checkout) actually works.
subject: Web Development

question: (Conceptual) What does the "Call Stack" tell a developer when a JavaScript error occurs?

options.label: A
options.text: How much memory the program is using.

options.label: B
options.text: The sequence of function calls that led to the current point of execution or the error.

options.label: C
options.text: The current CPU temperature.

options.label: D
options.text: The number of clicks performed by the user.

explanation:
The call stack helps trace the "origin" of a bug. It shows the chain of functions called (e.g.,
submitForm called validate called checkEmail), showing exactly where in the chain the
error occurred.
subject: Web Development

question: (Scenario-Based) A developer notices their CSS changes aren't appearing on the live site, even though they refreshed the page. What is the most likely cause?

options.label: A
options.text: The HTML is corrupt.

options.label: B
options.text: The browser is serving a cached version of the CSS file.

options.label: C
options.text: The computer needs a reboot.

options.label: D
options.text: JavaScript is blocking the CSS.

explanation:
Browsers aggressively cache CSS files for performance. A standard refresh might not force a
fetch of a new version. Developers can force a refresh or use "Disable Cache" in the DevTools
Network panel.
subject: Web Development

question: (Code/Logic) What is a "Mock" or "Stub" in the context of unit testing a backend API call?

options.label: A
options.text: A way to hack the server.

options.label: B
options.text: A tool to measure CPU usage.

options.label: C
options.text: A dummy object/function that mimics the real server response so tests can run without actual network calls.

options.label: D
options.text: A tool to rewrite the database queries.

subject: Web Development

question: (Conceptual) What is the primary benefit of Automated Testing in a CI/CD pipeline?

options.label: A
options.text: It makes the code more readable.

options.label: B
options.text: It ensures that every code change is validated immediately, preventing regression bugs from reaching production.

options.label: C
options.text: It replaces the need for UI design.

options.label: D
options.text: It allows the developers to work from home.

explanation:
Automated testing (CI) provides a "safety net." If a developer pushes a code change that
breaks something elsewhere, the automated pipeline fails, preventing the deployment of
broken software.
subject: Web Development

question: (Scenario-Based) You are inspecting a JavaScript Memory Leak. Which DevTools tab would help you find which objects are taking up the most RAM?

options.label: A
options.text: Sources

options.label: B
options.text: Network

options.label: C
options.text: Memory (Heap Snapshot)

options.label: D
options.text: Application

explanation:
The Memory tab allows you to take "Heap Snapshots." By comparing two snapshots taken at
different times, you can identify objects that were created but never deleted (leaked).
subject: Web Development

question: (Conceptual) What does "Headless" Testing mean?

options.label: A
options.text: Testing on devices without screens.

options.label: B
options.text: Running browser-based tests without a visible user interface (usually for faster CI/CD pipelines).

options.label: C
options.text: Testing without writing any code.

options.label: D
options.text: Testing without using an internet connection.

explanation:
"Headless" browsers (like Headless Chrome) run the browser engine in the background
without launching the UI. This is much faster for running thousands of E2E tests on a build
server.
subject: Web Development

question: (Comparison) What is the difference between TDD (Test-Driven Development) and standard testing?

options.label: A
options.text: TDD is only used for backend.

options.label: B
options.text: In TDD, tests are written *before* the code; standard testing writes tests *after* (or during) development.

options.label: C
options.text: TDD is easier to implement.

options.label: D
options.text: Standard testing requires fewer steps.

explanation:
TDD changes the mindset. You define the requirement as a test first, ensuring that every
piece of production code has a clear purpose and a corresponding test from the start.
subject: Web Development

question: (Conceptual) What is the main goal of Continuous Deployment (CD) in a DevOps pipeline?

options.label: A
options.text: To ensure developers spend all day fixing bugs.

options.label: B
options.text: To automate the release process so that every code change that passes automated tests is immediately deployed to production.

options.label: C
options.text: To manually approve every single line of code before it ships.

options.label: D
options.text: To hide production issues from the users.

explanation:
Continuous Deployment reduces the "lead time to production." By automating the pipeline,
software updates are released frequently and in small, manageable chunks, which is safer
than massive, infrequent releases.
subject: Web Development

question: (Scenario-Based) A startup wants to deploy their Node.js app but doesn't want to manage Linux server updates, firewalls, or patches. They just want to upload their code and have it run. Which model should they choose?

options.label: A
options.text: IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service)

options.label: B
options.text: PaaS (Platform as a Service)

options.label: C
options.text: On-Premise Data Center

options.label: D
options.text: Bare Metal Server

explanation:
PaaS (like Heroku, Vercel, or Render) abstracts away the server/OS management, letting
developers focus purely on code. IaaS requires the developer to manage the virtual machine's
OS and security.
subject: Web Development

question: (Code/Logic) What does a Dockerfile primarily achieve in a production deployment? Dockerfile FROM node:18 COPY . /app

options.label: A
options.text: It compiles JavaScript into binary C++ code.

options.label: B
options.text: It defines a reproducible environment (OS + Dependencies + Code) so the app runs the same on any machine.

options.label: C
options.text: It automatically hacks the server to gain root access.

options.label: D
options.text: It forces the code to run in a web browser.

explanation:
Containers (Docker) bundle the app with all its specific dependencies (e.g., Node version 18),
eliminating the "it works on my machine" problem.
subject: Web Development

question: (Conceptual) Which strategy involves running two identical production environments (Blue and Green), where only one is live at a time, allowing for instant rollback if a deployment fails?

options.label: A
options.text: Rollback Testing

options.label: B
options.text: Disaster Recovery

options.label: C
options.text: Blue-Green Deployment

options.label: D
options.text: Database Sharding

explanation:
In Blue-Green deployment, you deploy the new code (Green) while the old code (Blue) is live.
Once Green is verified, you switch the router to point all traffic to Green. If a bug is found, you
switch back to Blue in seconds.
subject: Web Development

question: (Scenario-Based) A website is experiencing massive traffic spikes during a sale. Which scaling technique is specifically designed to add more servers to a cluster automatically to handle this load?

options.label: A
options.text: Vertical Scaling (Scale-up)

options.label: B
options.text: Horizontal Scaling (Scale-out)

options.label: C
options.text: Normalization

options.label: D
options.text: Minification

explanation:
Horizontal scaling (adding more nodes) is the standard for web apps because there is a
physical limit to how much RAM/CPU one server can hold (Vertical scaling).
subject: Web Development

question: (Code/Console Logic) What is the purpose of this command in a deployment pipeline? RUN npm install CMD ["node", "app.js"]

options.label: A
options.text: Installs tools to help developers write code.

options.label: B
options.text: Installs only the dependencies needed to run the app, excluding dev-tools like testing frameworks to save space/time.

options.label: C
options.text: Installs the most recent beta version of the app.

options.label: D
options.text: Installs a virus scanner.

explanation:
In production, we don't need test runners or build tools like jest or eslint. Installing only
production dependencies makes the deployment package smaller and faster.
subject: Web Development

question: (Conceptual) What is a Canary Deployment?

options.label: A
options.text: Testing the software on birds.

options.label: B
options.text: Deploying to all servers at once.

options.label: C
options.text: Rolling out the update to a small subset of users first to monitor for issues before deploying to everyone.

options.label: D
options.text: Forcing every user to update their browser.

explanation:
Named after the "canary in a coal mine," this strategy mitigates risk by exposing a new feature
to only 5% of users. If the logs are clean, you roll it out to the other 95%.
subject: Web Development

question: (Comparison) What is the difference between IaaS and FaaS (Serverless)?

options.label: A
options.text: IaaS is free; FaaS is paid.

options.label: B
options.text: IaaS provides raw hardware/VMs (you manage OS); FaaS provides a container to run functions (you manage only code).

options.label: C
options.text: FaaS requires a dedicated server rack.

options.label: D
options.text: IaaS is always faster.

explanation:
IaaS (AWS EC2) gives you a "virtual computer" you must manage. FaaS (AWS Lambda) lets
you upload a single function, and the cloud provider handles EVERYTHING, charging you
only for the milliseconds the code runs.
subject: Web Development

question: (Conceptual) What is Infrastructure as Code (IaC)? bash - ci_pipeline $ npm install --only=production

options.label: A
options.text: Using JavaScript to style web pages.

options.label: B
options.text: Managing server setups, networks, and databases using configuration files (like Terraform) instead of manual UI clicks.

options.label: C
options.text: Storing code on a hard drive.

options.label: D
options.text: Automating unit tests.

explanation:
IaC treats server provisioning like software development. You check the server config into Git,
making the infrastructure version-controlled, testable, and reproducible.
subject: Web Development

question: (Scenario-Based) A deployment is failing because the production database has an environment variable DB_PASS set to "prod_secret", but the code is looking for DATABASE_PASSWORD. What went wrong?

options.label: A
options.text: The server doesn't have internet access.

options.label: B
options.text: Environment variable mismatch (configuration drift between code and server).

options.label: C
options.text: The code is missing a CSS file.

options.label: D
options.text: The database is offline.

explanation:
Configuration drift or mismatch is a classic deployment failure. The code expects a specific
key name, and if the environment provides a different one, the app cannot initialize.
subject: Web Development

question: (Conceptual) What is the primary difference between REST and SOAP?

options.label: A
options.text: REST is more secure than SOAP.

options.label: B
options.text: SOAP is only for JavaScript; REST is for Python.

options.label: C
options.text: REST is an architectural style based on resources; SOAP is a rigid protocol based on XML and WSDL.

options.label: D
options.text: REST requires more bandwidth than SOAP.

explanation:
REST is lightweight and flexible, often using JSON. SOAP is highly structured, XML-based,
and includes strict "contract" definitions (WSDL), making it heavier but more feature-rich for
enterprise integration.
subject: Web Development

question: (Scenario-Based) A mobile app developer wants to fetch data from a public API. Which HTTP method should they use to safely retrieve a list of products without causing any side effects?

options.label: A
options.text: GET

options.label: B
options.text: POST

options.label: C
options.text: PUT

options.label: D
options.text: PATCH

explanation:
GET is the "Safe" method. According to the HTTP spec, it should only be used to retrieve data
and should never modify the state of the server (e.g., it shouldn't delete or insert records).
subject: Web Development

question: (Code-Tracing) The following JSON is returned from an API. If you want to access the "lat" value using JavaScript, which path is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: response.lat

options.label: B
options.text: response.location.lat()

options.label: C
options.text: response.location.lat

options.label: D
options.text: response.location[lat]

explanation:
The lat key is a property inside the location object. The correct access path is dot
notation: object.property.nested_property.
subject: Web Development

question: (Conceptual) What does the "HATEOAS" principle in REST stand for?

options.label: A
options.text: Hypertext Access To Everything And Over All Systems.

options.label: B
options.text: Hypermedia As The Engine Of Application State.

options.label: C
options.text: Handling All Tasks Every Once A Second.

options.label: D
options.text: High Availability Through Extensible API Server.

explanation:
HATEOAS means the API includes links in the response (e.g., "next_page": "/api/users?
page=2"). This allows the client to navigate the API dynamically without knowing the URL
structure beforehand.
subject: Web Development

question: (Scenario-Based) A client-side application is trying to fetch data from https:// api.payments.com, but the browser blocks it and throws a CORS Error. Why?

options.label: A
options.text: The server is down.

options.label: B
options.text: The server at api.payments.com did not send the required "Access-Control- Allow-Origin" header to permit the client's origin.

options.label: C
options.text: The client's JavaScript has a syntax error.

options.label: D
options.text: The API is deprecated.

subject: Web Development

question: (Conceptual) Which of the following is a main advantage of GraphQL over traditional REST?

options.label: A
options.text: It uses fewer CPU cycles on the server.

options.label: B
options.text: It allows the client to specify exactly what fields it needs, preventing "over- fetching."

options.label: C
options.text: It automatically encrypts the database.

options.label: D
options.text: It is only compatible with mobile apps.

explanation:
In REST, you get exactly what the endpoint provides (which is often too much data). GraphQL
lets the frontend request specifically { name, id }, saving bandwidth and improving
frontend performance.
subject: Web Development

question: (Conceptual) What is a Webhook?

options.label: A
options.text: A way to hang a server.

options.label: B
options.text: A mechanism where the server "pushes" data to a client-provided URL whenever a specific event occurs.

options.label: C
options.text: A tool for website design.

options.label: D
options.text: A deprecated HTML tag.

explanation:
Webhooks are "reverse APIs." Instead of you polling the server ("Are there updates?"), the
server calls your URL when something happens (e.g., "A payment was just received").
subject: Web Development

question: (Scenario-Based) You need to upload a large binary file (e.g., a 100MB video) to a server. Which HTTP method is most appropriate?

options.label: A
options.text: GET

options.label: B
options.text: POST

options.label: C
options.text: HEAD

options.label: D
options.text: OPTIONS

explanation:
POST is designed for submitting data, including large binary streams (multipart/form-data).
GET is limited by URL length and is not designed for data uploads.
subject: Web Development

question: (Conceptual) What is the purpose of an API Key header?

options.label: A
options.text: To compress the API response.

options.label: B
options.text: To authenticate the client application calling the API.

options.label: C
options.text: To identify the user's browser.

options.label: D
options.text: To format the JSON.

explanation:
API Keys are a form of identity verification. By including a key in the header, the server knows
who is calling the API and can enforce usage limits or deny access if the key is invalid.
subject: Web Development

question: (Conceptual) What does Rate Limiting protect against?

options.label: A
options.text: Data leakage via XSS.

options.label: B
options.text: API abuse, scraping, or Denial of Service (DoS) attacks by restricting the number of requests per user/IP.

options.label: C
options.text: Poor CSS styling.

options.label: D
options.text: The N+1 problem.

explanation:
Rate limiting ensures one malicious or buggy client doesn't consume all your server
resources, which would make the API unusable for everyone else.
subject: Web Development

question: (Conceptual) What is the primary purpose of a Service Worker in a PWA?

options.label: A
options.text: To make the website load faster on desktops.

options.label: B
options.text: To act as a proxy between the browser and the network, enabling offline functionality and background sync.

options.label: C
options.text: To host the database for the application.

options.label: D
options.text: To execute heavy AI models on the server.

explanation:
Service Workers are event-driven scripts that run independently of the web page. They
intercept network requests, cache responses, and allow the app to work when the user is
offline.
subject: Web Development

question: (Comparison) What is the main advantage of Static Site Generation (SSG) compared to Server-Side Rendering (SSR)?

options.label: A
options.text: SSG is always more secure than SSR.

options.label: B
options.text: SSG files can be served from a CDN without any server-side logic, making them extremely fast and cheap to host.

options.label: C
options.text: SSG can update data in real-time.

options.label: D
options.text: SSG allows you to use PHP on the server.

explanation:
Since SSG generates all pages at build-time, you don't need a backend server running during
user visits. You just host the files on a CDN (like S3 or Netlify), which is effectively free and
instant.
subject: Web Development

question: (Conceptual) Which technology allows a C++ or Rust application to run inside a standard web browser?

options.label: A
options.text: jQuery

options.label: B
options.text: TypeScript

options.label: C
options.text: WebAssembly (Wasm)

options.label: D
options.text: Service Workers

explanation:
WebAssembly is a low-level, binary-format language for the web. It enables high-performance
applications (like Photoshop Web or Figma) to run in the browser using code originally written
in systems languages.
subject: Web Development

question: (Scenario-Based) You want to build a reusable component called <user-card> that works in any framework (React, Vue, or Vanilla JS). Which standard should you follow?

options.label: A
options.text: Node.js modules

options.label: B
options.text: Web Components (Custom Elements & Shadow DOM)

options.label: C
options.text: CSS Modules

options.label: D
options.text: Global jQuery plugins

explanation:
Web Components are a browser-native standard. Unlike React components, which only work
in React, Web Components are standard HTML elements that work in any browser without
dependencies.
subject: Web Development

question: (Conceptual) What is a Headless CMS?

options.label: A
options.text: A CMS that doesn't have an admin panel.

options.label: B
options.text: A CMS that provides content via an API, leaving the frontend rendering entirely to the developer.

options.label: C
options.text: A CMS that stores data on a USB stick.

options.label: D
options.text: A CMS that only works with XML.

explanation:
A traditional CMS (like old WordPress) controls both the database AND the visual theme. A
Headless CMS only cares about the database/content; it sends that data to your frontend
(React/Vue/Mobile) via API.
subject: Web Development

question: (Code/Logic) What does the Shadow DOM provide to Web Components?

options.label: A
options.text: Higher resolution for images.

options.label: B
options.text: Encapsulation, ensuring the component's internal CSS/HTML doesn't clash with the rest of the page.

options.label: C
options.text: A shadow effect behind the component.

options.label: D
options.text: Access to the user's microphone.

explanation:
Shadow DOM creates a scoped tree. CSS defined inside a Shadow DOM cannot style
elements outside of it, and external CSS cannot influence the elements inside, solving the
"global style" problem.
subject: Web Development

question: (Conceptual) Which of the following is a core characteristic of Micro-Frontends?

options.label: A
options.text: Combining all CSS into one huge file.

options.label: B
options.text: Breaking a large frontend application into smaller, independent apps that can be developed and deployed by different teams.

options.label: C
options.text: Running the entire frontend on the server.

options.label: D
options.text: Using only one framework for the whole site.

explanation:
Micro-frontends allow large organizations to have one team managing the "Cart" (in React)
and another team managing the "Product Catalog" (in Vue), all within the same user
experience.
subject: Web Development

question: (Scenario-Based) A developer is optimizing a PWA (Progressive Web App). They want the app to be "Installable" on a phone's home screen. Which file must they include?

options.label: A
options.text: package.json

options.label: B
options.text: index.php

options.label: C
options.text: manifest.json

options.label: D
options.text: robots.txt

explanation:
The manifest.json file tells the mobile OS the app's name, icons, and theme colors, which
enables the "Add to Home Screen" functionality.
subject: Web Development

question: (Conceptual) What is Hydration (in the context of modern React/Next.js)?

options.label: A
options.text: Downloading images from the cloud.

options.label: B
options.text: Attaching JavaScript event listeners to server-rendered HTML so the page becomes interactive.

options.label: C
options.text: Saving the user's session to a cookie.

options.label: D
options.text: Compressing the JavaScript bundle.

explanation:
SSR renders HTML on the server. That HTML is a "dead" document. Hydration is the process
where the JS framework takes control of that HTML in the browser to add interactivity.
subject: Web Development

question: (Conceptual) What is the main benefit of using TypeScript in modern web development?

options.label: A
options.text: It makes web browsers faster.

options.label: B
options.text: It provides static type checking for JavaScript, preventing type-related bugs during development.

options.label: C
options.text: It automatically converts HTML to JSON.

options.label: D
options.text: It replaces the need for CSS.

explanation:
TypeScript adds interfaces and types to JS. It is "compiled" back to plain JS. This catches
errors (like user.id being undefined) before the code ever runs.
subject: Web Development
